newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF ARSENAL SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF ARSENAL SQUAD.

text.p: Pen pictures of players expected to comprise the Arsenal squad for Saturday's English premier league match against Aston Villa:

David Seaman, goalkeeper, 33. Became a national hero in the summer with a series of fine performances and crucial penalty saves for England during Euro '96. Joined Arsenal from QPR for 1.3 million pounds ($2.2 million) (then a record fee for a goalkeeper) in the summer of 1990. Currently out of the side with three cracked ribs but could be close to a return.
John Lukic, goalkeeper, Age 36. Now in his second spell at Arsenal, veteran Lukic is David Seaman's understudy. Was Arsenal's first choice keeper between 1986-90 before leaving for Leeds.

Lee Dixon, defender, 32. Joined Arsenal from Stoke nearly nine years ago and played a key part in Arsenal's championship and cup successes of the late 1980s and early 1990s. Missed last week's defeat at Nottingham Forest because of an ankle injury.
Nigel Winterburn, defender, 33. Left-back and another key member of Arsenal's successes under George Graham. Although 33 seems in no danger of losing his place yet.

Martin Keown, defender, 30. Versatile defender who captains the side in Tony Adam's absence. Voted Arsenal's Player of the Season by their fans and just awarded a pay rise and new contract by the club.

Tony Adams, defender, 30. Suspended from last week's match at Forest, Mr Arsenal will be back for Saturday's match in place of Andy Linighan. Became one of Arsenal's youngest ever skippers in 1988 and is among the all-time favourites of the Highbury crowd. Admitted serious problems with alcohol earlier in the season but has rarely looked as impressive on the pitch as he currently does.

Steve Bould, defender, 34. Like Adams, has been at the heart of the Arsenal defence for most of the last decade, although thigh and groin injuries over the years have kept him out of the side for long periods. Tall, commanding and despite his advancing years, still Adams first choice partner.
Andy Linighan, defender, 34. Able deputy for Bould or Adams. Played against Forest last week but likely to make way for Adams' return.
Gavin McGowan, defender, 20. A rare man at Highbury -- an Arsenal defender not in his 30s. Reserve full-back who played against Forest last week but likely to be on the bench again if Dixon is fit.

Patrick Vieira, defender-midfielder, 20. Wonderfully balanced and talented Senegal-born youngster who began his career at Cannes in France and joined Arsenal for 3.0 million pounds from AC Milan in July. His reading of the game and passing has had a major impact in Arsenal's good form this season. Hot-headed and rash behaviour tends to get him into trouble, but he could well develop into one of the game's greats.

Remi Garde, midfielder-sweeper, 30. A free-signing from Strasbourg at the start of the season, he made his first start against Forest on Saturday in place of suspended compatriot Patrick Vieira. Likely to be substitute again on Saturday. Has won six France caps.

Ray Parlour, midfielder, 23. Erratic, curly-haired midfielder who has been in and out of the side since making his senior debut for Arsenal as an 18-year-old in 1992. On his day a potential match-winner.

Steve Morrow, midfielder, 26. Scored Arsenal's winner in the 1993 League Cup win over Sheffield Wednesday -- then broke his arm celebrating the victory afterwards. Northern Ireland international with nearly 100 Arsenal appearances to his name but never really won an established place in the side.

Paul Merson, midfielder, 28. Now playing some of the best football of his career after his much-publicised admissions of alcoholism and drug abuse. An ever-present last season. One of the most talented players in England.

David Platt, midfielder, 30. Joined Arsenal for 4.75 million pounds from Sampdoria in 1995 which took his combined transfer fees throughout his career to a staggering 17.0 million pounds. But his form at Arsenal has rarely risen above average and his hard-running game has produced very few goals. Scored 50 league goals in 121 matches for Aston Villa in the late 1980s. Recently linked with a move to Blackburn.

Dennis Bergkamp, forward, 27. Arsenal's record signing cost 7.5 million pounds from Inter Milan in the summer of 1995 and the Dutchman has forged a dangerous partnership with Ian Wright in attack. Superb skills, superb goalscorer, one of the best overseas players currently playing in England.

John Hartson, forward, 24. Tall, powerfully built Welsh international who always poses problems for opposing defences whenever he gets a first-team chance, which this season has mainly been restricted to the last 20 minutes as substitute.

Ian Wright, forward, 33. Fast closing in on Cliff Bastin's 60-year-old all-time club scoring record of 178 goals, Wright now has 164. Has lost none of his venom in front of goal and has already scored 21 times this season. But his volatile temper often lands him in trouble as it did last week at Forest when he was sent off after scoring in the Gunners 2- 1 defeat. A further booking during the holiday period could see him banned for five matches in January.
